The relief sought for in the present writ petition is to direct the respondents 2 and 3 to consider the petitioner's representation dated on 02.09.2022 and subsequently direct the respondents 2 and 3 to pay the compensation amount of Rs.29,70,044/- to the petitioner.
2 . I t i s n o t i n d i s p u t e b e t w e e n t h e p a r t i e s t h a t t h e S u b j e c t l a n d s w e r e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis acquired by the National Highways Authority of India for expansion of road projects.
The procedures contemplated under the National Highways Act, 1956 were followed by the authorities and the quantum of compensation to be paid to the landholders were determined and paid accordingly.
3. The very relief sought for in the present writ petition is to direct the respondents 2 and 3 to settle the compensation in favour of the petitioner.

4. The respective learned counsels appearing on behalf of the respondents brought to the notice of this Court that the compensation has already been settled pursuant to the award in favour of the 5 th respondent.

If at all any dispute exists between the petitioner and the 5 th respondent, it is to be construed as a private dispute and parties have to approach the Civil Court for resolving the issues.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner made a submission that the petitioner is the absolute owner and he has got documents to establish his rights.
That being the case, the petitioner has to approach the Competent Civil Court for the purpose of resolving the issues.

As far as the 2 nd https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent is concerned, the land acquisition proceedings were completed and the compensation determined was also settled in favour of the landholders.
